source.title: Attention Sensitivity Is Not Enough: Dissociating Attention-Level and Behavioural In-Context Learning under Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Jin-Yuan Zhang; Peng-Ji He; He-Long Hu; Yin Yuan; Sheng-Shuo Jiao

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; full paper text including appendices is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests behavioural in-context learning under fine-tuning with matched-versus-mismatched accuracy gaps, alongside a different attention-sensitivity proxy; it does not identify or intervene on induction heads.
record.gate_note: The paper cites induction heads as background but does not measure their formation, composition, or copying behaviour. It also does not test an induction-head transition against a loss bump. Rows record the paper's own behavioural ICL and attention-sensitivity results; cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Induction heads appear only as background motivation for attention diagnostics. The study never identifies, measures or ablates induction or previous-token heads, and never tracks head formation or a loss bump. Its behavioural measure is a few-shot matched-minus-permuted label-accuracy gap under fine-tuning of Llama-2-7B. That is a related but different construct from the in-context learning score (loss falling with token index) that V2, V3 and V5 name. It also does not attribute that gap to any mechanism, so it cannot bear on V6. The fine-tuning arms do not show ICL depending on the setup in the sense of V5. The random-label gap stays positive in every arm. The pretrained QA gap is never reported, so loss of QA ICL through fine-tuning cannot be assessed. The ICS arm deliberately optimises an attention divergence, which induces the attention behaviour rather than observing it arise. The results belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that maximising the ICS attention divergence saturates it near √2 while the controlled QA ICL-GAP stays near zero and MMLU drops 0.371→0.279. They also conclude that mild behavioural gating only partially mitigates this, and that anchored objectives keep MMLU near pretrained. Their stated lesson is that attention proxies need behavioural validation before use as training targets.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes Llama-2-7B and measures matched-versus-mismatched attention-row distance and behavioural accuracy gaps; it does not use the original induction-head identification or training-phase analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured behavioural gap differs between the random-label and controlled QA probe protocols. Results are also reported for different fine-tuning objectives, B-ICS gate settings, and AnchorTune coefficients; only one main model and training mixture are used.

fits_no_version.finding: An ICS-maximising objective drives the attention divergence to 1.413 (ceiling ≈1.414) while the controlled QA ICL-GAP stays near zero and MMLU falls from 0.371 to 0.279. Attention becomes sharp and disjoint but routes to formatting or demonstration-body tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matched-vs-mismatched attention sensitivity is not a reliable target for preserving behavioural ICL under optimisation.

fits_no_version.finding: The few-shot random-label matched-vs-permuted gap in Llama-2-7B (0.306 pretrained) stays positive after 5,000 fine-tuning steps in all four arms (0.188–0.352). The controlled QA gap is near zero in every fine-tuned arm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural few-shot label-mapping ICL in a 7B model largely survives instruction fine-tuning regardless of which parameters are frozen.

fits_no_version.finding: Anchoring to pretrained computation (attention rows, logits, weights, or LM head) keeps MMLU near pretrained, while ICL-GAP stays near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anchored fine-tuning objectives preserve general ability better than divergence-maximising attention objectives.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one base model, one main probe design and training mixture, one demonstration count, and mostly single-seed baselines. The controlled QA trajectory uses 200 paired examples per checkpoint, whereas the fixed evaluation set contains 500 pairs. The authors note the MMLU probe has 240 items and leave controlled unregularised-collapse testing for future work. No induction heads are directly identified or tested.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported behavioural ICL outcomes relevant to V5 were omitted. MMLU accuracy and ECE are not behavioural ICL-gap measures; other attention and capability-preservation results not directly bearing on the claim versions are omitted.

untested.parts: Induction heads, composition with previous-token heads, [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying.
Head formation timing, abruptness, loss bump, coincidence with an ICL gain.
Attribution of ICL in large models to induction heads.
Induction heads across families, sizes, runs or architectures; only Llama-2-7B is used and no heads are identified.
Dependence of induction-head formation or ICL-score persistence on data or training; only a few-shot label gap under fine-tuning is measured, and it does not vary meaningfully across arms.
Which mechanisms carry few-shot task learning; no head-level attribution is done.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V5 on the basis of 'ICL persistence depends on setup'. However, the measured ICL is a few-shot label-accuracy gap with no link to induction heads. It is also largely unchanged across arms, and the pretrained controlled-QA gap is never reported. Several reader states are off: 'partial' for gaps the authors call within ±0.04 of zero, and 'reversed' for -0.015 to -0.020 values within a noise scale of about 0.046. Rows R15–R24 are the study's own method comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Induction heads, previous-token-head composition, and [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying.

Induction-head formation, abruptness of formation, a training-loss bump, and whether head formation coincides with an ICL gain. The paper tracks behavioural ICL and an attention-divergence proxy, not induction heads.
Whether induction heads carry most ICL in large transformers; no induction-head attribution or large-model comparison is performed.
Generality across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities; only Llama-2-7B is studied.

The study tests behavioural ICL across probe protocols and fine-tuning objectives on one model and one main training mixture. It does not test induction-head formation, broad variation in training data, or whether ICL persists across model families.
Whether few-shot task learning is carried mainly by mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Random-label protocol across pretrained and 5,000-step fine-tuned checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Matched demonstrations yield positive gaps across the tested label pairs and all four fine-tuned arms (R1-R7), showing behavioural ICL persists under this probe protocol.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Controlled QA probe and fine-tuning-objective variants
reader_labels.reason: The controlled QA gap is near zero or slightly negative across several arms while the random-label probe remains positive; mild B-ICS yields only a small positive gap, and anchor variants also have near-zero gaps (R8-R24). Results therefore depend on probe and training setup, and do not establish broad data dependence.
